newsitem.title: USA: Former Dyno Nobel exec charged by US Justice Dept.
newsitem.headline: Former Dyno Nobel exec charged by US Justice Dept.

text.p: A former executive of Dyno Nobel Inc, a unit of Norway's Dyno Industrier ASA, was charged on Wednesday with rigging bids on commercial explosives contracts sold to two companies, the Department of Justice said.
The one-count criminal case was filed in the U.S. District Court in Dallas against Donald Westmaas, Dyno Nobel's vice president of marketing until 1993.
The case charged that Westmaas and co-conspiritors agreed to rig certain 1992 dynamite contracts to metal mining company The Doe Run Co and to ASARCO Inc, which has lead mines in Missouri.
The purpose of the conspiracy was to allow Dyno Nobel and co-conspiritors to submit bids that were artifically higher than they should have been, the Department of Justice said.

"The Antitrust Division will vigorously prosecute anyone who undermines the Sherman Act by fixing prices or rigging bids," said Joel Klein, Assistant Attorney General in charge of the Department's Antitrust Division.
The charge results from an ongoing antitrust investigation of the explosives and ammonium nitrate industries.
